title: Dismissible suggested prompts
one_liner: Users can hide individual suggested prompt cards by long-pressing or right-clicking them, and the remaining suggestions refresh.

prd.problem: Suggested prompts shown to users may be irrelevant or repetitive, and users have no way to remove them.
prd.users: Gemini web users who see suggestion cards on the start screen.
prd.what: Each suggestion card gets a hidden options affordance, revealed by long-press or context menu, with a 'Hide' action. Hiding a card announces 'Suggestion hidden.' to screen readers. If replacement suggestions load, it announces 'Suggestion hidden. Suggestions updated.'
prd.how_it_appears: Suggestion cards in a 'Suggested prompts' group on the Gemini home or empty-chat screen. The card button handles click, contextmenu and focus events, and has a 'dismissBubble' element labelled 'Hide'.
prd.rollout_guess: Likely a quiet UI change with no announcement. The chunk is new to us, so this may already exist in some form.
open_questions: Is this already live and just new to our crawl?
Does hiding persist across sessions or only last for the current view?

title: SIEM connection for Enterprise workspaces
one_liner: Admins can connect Notion to a SIEM tool and manage that connection from Settings → Connections.

evidence.text: You can manage your SIEM connection in Settings → Connections.

prd.problem: Security teams want Notion activity and audit data streamed into their SIEM for monitoring and compliance.
prd.users: Enterprise workspace owners and security admins.
prd.what: A flow to connect a SIEM. It ends in a success confirmation, and the connection is then managed under Settings → Connections.
prd.how_it_appears: A success modal or toast with a 'Manage connection' button and a 'Done' button. The connection is managed in the Settings → Connections page.
prd.rollout_guess: Enterprise-only. Likely announced in release notes or the security and admin docs, possibly gated to a small set of customers first.
open_questions: Which SIEM vendors are supported (Splunk, Datadog, Sentinel, etc.)?
Is this a new audit-log streaming feature or a repackaging of the existing audit log export?

title: API and MCP token expiry warning notifications
one_liner: Users get notified before an API or MCP connection token expires, with the connection name and expiry date.

evidence.text: The API token for {connectionName} expires on {expiresOn}.
The MCP token for {connectionName} expires on {expiresOn}.

prd.problem: Integration and MCP tokens that expire silently break automations and agent connections.
prd.users: Workspace admins and developers who own integrations or MCP connections.
prd.what: A notification, keyed to a bot token, that warns the owner before the token expires. The wording differs for API tokens and MCP tokens.
prd.how_it_appears: A notification in the inbox or notification center, probably linking to the connection settings.
prd.rollout_guess: Likely ships quietly alongside token expiry or rotation controls for connections. It may or may not appear in release notes.
open_questions: Is there a setting for the token lifetime?
How far ahead of expiry is the warning sent?

title: Split pull request with agent
one_liner: Ask an agent in Linear Reviews to break a large pull request into a stack of smaller, dependent pull requests.

evidence.text: Keep part 1 in this pull request. Put each later part on its own stacked branch, with a pull request based on the part below it. Keep the total changes the same, and adjust the parts where the code calls for it.

prd.problem: Large pull requests are hard to review.
prd.users: Developers and reviewers using Linear Reviews.
prd.what: A review action that has an agent propose parts of the change and then create stacked branches and pull requests, with part 1 kept in the current pull request.
prd.how_it_appears: Action in the review or command menu, with keywords split, stack, smaller and break up.
prd.rollout_guess: Inferred: ships as part of the Reviews and agent feature set, possibly behind a flag at first.
open_questions: Is it available to all Reviews users or only some plans?
Does it need the cloud coding agent to push branches?

title: Private and shared documents
one_liner: Create private documents visible only to you and share them with specific people, with a 30-day trash for deleted private documents.

evidence.text: Deleted private documents stay here for 30 days

prd.problem: Documents are tied to teams, projects and initiatives, with no personal drafting space.
prd.what: Personal documents with per-person sharing and a trash view.
prd.how_it_appears: A 'Create private document' action and a private documents trash view, gated by the personalAndSharedDocuments flag.
prd.rollout_guess: Inferred: gradual rollout and a changelog entry.
open_questions: Can guests be invited to private documents?

title: Cloud coding agent admin controls (region pinning, commit signing, inference)
one_liner: Workspace admins can pin cloud coding agent sandboxes to the US or EU, require signed commits, and choose who provides inference.

evidence.text: Pin new cloud coding agent sandboxes to the US. Region pinning raises the sandbox compute price.
EU workspaces always pin new cloud coding agent sandboxes to the EU. Region pinning raises the sandbox compute price.
Your workspace requires signed commits for cloud coding agents. Add a signing key to continue.
Choose who provides inference for cloud coding agents

prd.problem: Enterprise customers need data-residency, commit-integrity and model-provider control over cloud coding agents.
prd.users: Workspace admins and enterprise or EU customers.
prd.what: Settings under Cloud coding agent for sandbox region pinning at a higher compute price, commit signing keys, an inference provider choice, and team restrictions.
prd.rollout_guess: Inferred: some controls may already be in beta, so rollout could be incremental.
open_questions: Is region pinning a paid add-on?
Are these settings already live to some customers?

title: MCP team access controls
one_liner: Admins can restrict which teams MCP connections to Linear can access.

evidence.text: Choose which teams MCP connections can access. Workspace-level data, such as users and initiatives, stays available
Limit what MCP connections to Linear can access. These settings don't apply to Agent connectors

prd.problem: MCP connections currently have broad access across the workspace.
prd.what: A 'Team access' setting in Linear MCP server settings that scopes MCP access to selected teams.
prd.rollout_guess: Inferred: likely limited to higher plans.
open_questions: Does it also apply to API access?

title: Workbench for adding items from Linear AI
one_liner: The Linear agent can add items to a Workbench.

prd.what: An agent tool that adds items to a Workbench, a collection or workspace surface.
prd.how_it_appears: Agent tool-call labels in the Linear AI chat.
